items.summary: This is a concept I see used way less often than it should be used, in my opinion: How global or local a solution for a problem is. What does that mean? If you want to cross a river, swimming across it is a local solution. Building a bridge for others to use is a global solution. If you’re cold, putting on one more sweater is a local solution. Turning up your heating is a global solution. If you want to listen to music, putting in earphones is a local solution. Turning up the music on your phone is a global solution. If you’re ill, putting on a mask (or staying in your room) is a local solution, asking the choir to do their rehearsal outside is a (more) global solution. Locality and Globality lie on a spectrum. items.summary: arXiv:2611.34137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delta has been successfully employed as an authorship attribution method in various contexts, although its effectiveness is not always perfect. Since it is based on the most frequent words, its results can be readily interpreted and explained in plain English. In this study, we propose improving its performance by applying a resampling method to the selected stylistic features. The results show that this approach increases the accuracy of the model while preserving the interpretability of its outcomes. However, the main drawback of the proposed technique is the additional computational time required to obtain more accurate results.

items.summary: arXiv:2611.34830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated decision systems, from learned policies to model-based optimizers, often minimize costs such as energy or resource use while meeting a service requirement, for example the quality of service (QoS) specified in a service level agreement (SLA), a comfort band, or a safety margin. We study this choice in the Smart Buildings Challenge, in which a single policy controls the heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) of previously unseen buildings and is evaluated by a weighted sum of comfort, energy cost and carbon emissions. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in LLM-assisted theorem proving and program verification have attracted widespread attention. Drawing on interactive proof systems from computational complexity theory, we cast an LLM agent as the prover: under a designated protocol, the agent interacts with a formal verifier to substantiate its claimed answer to a problem instance. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When evidence is distributed across LLM agents, a team may collectively possess all the information needed for a decision yet fail to use it effectively. What must agents communicate for accurate joint predictions, and when does interaction help? Drawing on information theory and communication complexity, we develop a framework that combines theoretical benchmarks with controlled experiments and message-level analyses. items.summary: arXiv:2611.34852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. items.summary: arXiv:2611.34832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. We find that most proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control, such as preparation and prudent action, whereas proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe. items.summary: arXiv:2611.34536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents increasingly interact with one another, and many of these interactions are mixed-motive games, which have posed a persistent challenge for learning algorithms. Most multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms are designed to reach Nash equilibria, yet in many such games these equilibria are Pareto-inefficient. We instead study Kantian equilibria, an economic solution concept in which each agent plays the action it would want all agents to adopt. In symmetric games, this corresponds to an optimal common policy. We propose Kant-Q, a Q-learning algorithm in which each agent learns action profiles where all agents play the same action. Each update is then a sample from a single-agent MDP, so Kant-Q inherits the convergence guarantees of standard Q-learning. We show that…
items.title: Kant-Q: A Q-Learning Algorithm for Kantian Equilibrium in Symmetric Markov Games

items.summary: arXiv:2611.34147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quality control for proposition decomposition by large language models (LLMs) raises two asymmetric questions. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearest-neighbor methods are local, simple, and interpretable, but their non-parametric form makes them memory-intensive, expensive at inference, and difficult to integrate into differentiable neural architectures. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Barrier certificates provide formal safety guarantees for neural network controlled systems by ensuring that system trajectories avoid unsafe regions over time. items.summary: The Necessary Middleman Money has no inherent value by itself; it’s a social construct. Its value comes from the things you buy with it. Why did we create money? items.summary: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We formalize creative generation as a multi-objective distributional optimization problem and introduce SEPO, a training-free framework for System Prompt Ensemble Optimization. items.summary: Interpretable tool wear assessment in CNC machining is challenging. Existing diagnostic models have high accuracy but provide limited guidance for tool replacement. This study proposes a two layer framework combining deep learning wear classification and LLM assisted reasoning. The first layer uses PCA Loading feature selection and optimized GRU to recognize three wear states, achieving 98.38 percent macro F1 score on the PHM2010 dataset. The second layer uses LLMs to generate natural language reports and replacement suggestions from classification results and feature trends. Engineer evaluation shows the reports outperform rule templates. Cross dataset tests on NASA milling data support the generalizability of this framework.

items.summary: A conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. The system consists of the Navier-Stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion Maxwell--Stefan equations. The numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. First-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. Numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the convergence of the scheme and indicate second-order convergence in space in the $L^2$ norm.

items.summary: Summary: We may soon have autonomous AI researchers who choose their own research projects. Two agents picked at random chose the same project about 1 time in 60, against about 1 in 530 for people at AI safety hackathons, meaning agents duplicate each other about 8 times as often as people do. Agents from different labs mostly choose different projects, but agents from the same lab often choose the same ones, even with different models (about 1 time in 300 across labs, against at least 1 in 40 within a lab). Varying launch prompts helps only a little, varying harnesses not at all, and letting agents search the literature doubles the effective number of projects, but crowds agents onto one research area. Small interventions can spread them out…
items.title: AI research agents crowd onto the same projects, and how to spread them out

items.summary: [This is a link-post for https://transluce.org/posteriorbench. We recommend reading the website version for interactive visualizations.] Rare language model behaviors can be difficult to study, because obtaining them through ordinary sampling can take a very large number of samples. Alternatively, one can build a sampler that cheaply generates transcripts with a given behavior that are likely under the model. We introduce PosteriorBench, a benchmark that compares such sampling methods by their compute cost and how closely they match ground-truth model samples with a target behavior. We find that no method we evaluate is both efficient and faithful, and we hope PosteriorBench can measure progress toward one that is. Read the paper on arXiv, or get the code and data. items.summary: Abstract interpretation can certify properties of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), but precise analyses remain expensive. General implementations repeat work when analyzing the same architecture under different inputs and properties. Interleaving this work with numerical operations limits GPU utilization and restricts how much of the analysis a tensor compiler can process together. We present Scepter, a framework for specializing DNN abstract interpreters through structural semantics. The semantics determine the structure of intermediate abstract values while deferring their numerical evaluation. Structural computations from successive operations can therefore be performed together before certification, generating an executable tensor program. With the abstract interpreter and DNN architecture fixed, the program can be reused with different…
items.title: Fast and Scalable Abstract Interpretation for Deep Neural Networks

items.summary: Egocentric video question answering enables blind and low-vision (BLV) users to query their immediate surroundings through natural language. However, existing benchmarks and models primarily optimize for semantic agreement with reference answers, reducing visual assistance to a purely factual matching task. In real-world scenarios, a factually correct response remains practically unhelpful if it lacks the spatial orientation, actionable detail, or conciseness required by the immediate task of the user. Drawing upon real BLV egocentric videos and authentic user queries from EgoBlind, we construct the PA-EgoQA, a preference-aligned dataset that reconstructs reference answers according to empirical BLV communication criteria. items.summary: In this work, we extend the Intrinsic Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume method for the Intrinsic Shallow Water Equations (ISWE) to account for localized topographic discontinuities that influence flow patterns. The ISWE formulation is modified to incorporate these bottom perturbations without altering the global structure of the system. The numerical discretization is based on a Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume scheme within an intrinsic geometric framework and consists of a Lagrangian evolution step followed by an Eulerian remapping onto a fixed reference grid. The combination of the intrinsic nature of the ISWE formulation and the dual Lagrangian-Eulerian structure of the proposed discretization yields a numerical method that naturally satisfies the three key properties essential for stability, accuracy, and robustness…
items.title: A robust Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume scheme for intrinsic shallow water equations with wetting-and-drying transitions on locally discontinuous beds

items.summary: Alongside superposition, polysemanticity is one of the primary obstacles to achieving interpretable deep neural networks. While these phenomena are typically intrinsically linked, the Quadratic Programming Enhanced Model (QPM) naturally decouples them. By representing classes with a sparse binary assignment of very few features, QPM prevents superposition by design on its final features but still exhibits polysemanticity. However, measuring polysemanticity is an open problem. This work proposes a utility-focused approach to measuring polysemanticity by quantifying the decrease in interference-induced activation errors, which yields the practical utility of tighter prediction sets using Conformal Prediction (CP). We explicitly disentangle the polysemantic features of QPM into monosemantic concepts to create the Monosemantic QPM…
items.title: MonoQPM: Splitting Features into Concepts for Inherent Interpretability and Predictive Performance

items.summary: Independently pretrained vision and language models may learn shared structures of the same underlying world, providing a foundation for combining them to build multimodal capabilities. However, a key challenge remains in aligning cross-modal feature representations while preserving access to visual information before and after language adaptation. To this end, we propose sparse alignment with visual evidence-guided residual adaptation (SAVERA), a framework that combines frozen vision and language models through bidirectional alignment in a shared sparse space and prompt-guided residual fusion. items.summary: Image-text alignment serves as a foundation for modern vision-language models (VLMs), yet prevailing training paradigms provide limited supervision for learning how semantic changes correspond across modalities. To address this limitation, we propose a post-training method that learns cross-modal semantic change correspondences through controlled visual and textual variations. Specifically, we introduce a Semantic Difference Alignment (SDA) loss which can align the directions of corresponding visual and textual representation changes. We combine our proposed SDA with pairwise sigmoid matching to jointly learn image-text correspondences and cross-modal semantic changes, encouraging more fine-grained and discriminative visual representations. To support this learning, we construct VarFamily-40K, a dataset of image-text pairs with…

items.summary: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.
items.title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line

items.summary: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower decay relative to the capacity law above suggests that ensembles capture a growing share of epistemic uncertainty and become more competitive as an axis…
items.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models

We adapt emerging mechanistic interpretability methods to pinpoint and characterize model components that encode this bias. Specifically, we leverage multilingual bias benchmarks in implementing two methods for identifying social bias neurons: activation probability entropy and integrated gap gradients. We find the latter method to be more effective, as the neurons it isolates (which are largely concentrated at the model's deepest layers) lead to sharper decreases in model bias when suppressed. items.summary: A fallacy I keep seeing: "If AI automates all jobs, who will buy all the products?" "At some point they'll need to implement UBI so that consumer demand continues to exist", etc etc. Demand in itself isn't valuable. If you have a bunch of food, you can feed it to lions: they'll happily provide demand! But they won't give you much in exchange, so there's no point. Economic activity isn't about getting rid of stuff, it's about getting stuff in return. An AI company can consume resources, like energy for running the servers, same as a human can consume food. And the AI company can be contracted to do jobs, like a human, possibly for less resources per unit of work than a human. There's nothing that requires a human to "close the loop". items.summary: We address the problem of learning audio-visual representations from co-occurring modalities. Multimodal contrastive learning typically assumes that paired observations provide shared views of the same underlying information. While this may be true for datasets collected in constrained environments, it does not always hold. For instance, co-occurring audio and visual signals can differ substantially in their content due to off-screen sounds. Nevertheless, standard contrastive objectives treat all paired samples as equally aligned. In this work, we propose Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL), a model-agnostic objective that leverages modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between audio and video. CGAAL uses these agreement scores to weight the contribution of each positive pair. A warm-up period and gradual…

items.summary: OpenAI agents’ attack on Hugging Face this summer acted as a major warning shot. One particularly scary, and less noted, detail of this incident is how it helped later agents compromise OpenAI’s own infrastructure. The swarm of agents in the Hugging Face incident wrote down zero-day exploits, stolen credentials, techniques for faking records of their actions, and a way onto the open internet. Days later, after the original swarm ended, more advanced agents found its leftover credential-forging material in a shared cache and used it to escalate their privileges. From there, they eventually obtained admin access to an OpenAI research cluster. This illustrates one way current misalignment incidents[1] plausibly increase takeover risk. Agents can leave behind notes containing dangerous information, like credentials or strategies to subvert…

items.summary: UAV-mounted base stations (UxNBs) can provide ondemand 5G coverage, but their limited onboard energy makes power consumption the main operational constraint. AI-driven Open RAN controllers are a promising solution, yet they are trained almost exclusively on analytical models and simulations, since no public dataset captures the real energy behavior of a flying 5G base station (BS). As a first step toward closing this gap, we present a UAV testbed hosting a 5G picocell that supports a 20 MHz carrier and up to 100 Mbps throughput. The testbed measures BS system metrics, including power consumption, CPU load, and temperature, alongside UAV flight telemetry and detailed per-layer vRAN processing metrics. items.summary: TL;DR: Trained latent communication protocols allow LLMs to communicate with other LLMs without the need for text. However, we find that current state-of-the-art trained latent links carry little semantic content. These links can in fact affect safety - even benignly trained links cause refusal erosion in their receiver models, overriding safety guardrails, allowing LLMs to respond to harmful and dangerous prompts. We posit that the current latent communication paradigm is dangerous and ineffective. Why care? Latent communication is a form of neuralese : a way language models can communicate with each other without using human-readable text. items.summary: Existing clip-based soccer commentary models often produce delayed, repeated, or poorly synchronized narration on untrimmed full-match videos. Recent streaming video-language models make low-latency full-match narration feasible, but they often favor general descriptions rather than professional, event-grounded soccer commentary. They may describe nearby actions while failing to mention key events such as goals, cards, substitutions, and offsides correctly and on time. In this paper, we present SoccerNarrate to bridge low-latency streaming narration with event-grounded professional soccer commentary across data, training, and evaluation. First, we construct SoccerNarrate-Data, a large-scale time-anchored dataset with word-level ASR alignment, quality filtering, and entity calibration. items.summary: First-order reinforcement learning, such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), is widely used to post-train Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for multimodal reasoning. However, it incurs heavy memory and system overhead from backpropagation, optimizer states, and a reference model. Forward-only zeroth-order (ZO) methods, such as Evolution Strategies (ES) and its top-k variant Augmented Random Search (ARS), avoid these overheads via reward-guided weight perturbations, yet remain unexplored for VLM reasoning. We find that directly applying standard ES or vanilla ARS to VLMs suffers from two fundamental failure modes: (i) patch-grid overfitting, fitting fragile grid-specific visual token artifacts while ignoring spatial invariants, and (ii) catastrophic forgetting, degrading general perception and out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks due to…

items.summary: OpenAI recently published the base-model log-perplexity of 13 models it has trained since GPT-3.5, measured on a fixed held-out dataset sourced from its own codebase. It shows a very striking acceleration in pretraining loss: since early 2026, it has been falling about seven times faster than it was from 2022 through 2025. If the current pace holds, OpenAI would cover the drop in log-perplexity from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4.1, which took three years, in about six and a half months. This acceleration is even more striking because progress in loss should get harder over time: text is never perfectly predictable, so the loss can’t fall below some floor, and gains typically become smaller as models approach it. items.summary: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.

items.summary: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to reverse-engineer neural networks by identifying small, faithful subgraphs--circuits--that implement specific behaviors. In this work, we propose Spectral Circuit Analysis (SCA), a gradient-spectral pipeline that achieves consistent circuit discovery along both axes: stable across input formulations of the same task, and natively exposing structure shared across tasks. items.summary: One view of AI’s trajectory can be captured by this “fake graph” (with the gray region reflecting roughly where we are): AI is improving in intelligence while human intelligence is fixed. At some point AI will be so powerful that there is no way for humans to comprehend what it is doing, and hence at this point AI will necessarily take over control. The only question is whether the AI will be aligned (i.e. be a “benevolent dictator”) or misaligned (i.e., “if anyone builds it everyone dies”). Indeed, some people in the AI safety community view the former version of a “handover”, “handoff”, or “passing the torch” to AI as a positive outcome. I disagree with this view. items.summary: Large language models can have behaviours which only arise in hard-to-anticipate contexts. items.summary: Tuning a mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver is an instance-specific problem, where a poor configuration can increase solving time by orders of magnitude. Existing Bayesian optimization tuners treat solver tuning as a black-box optimization problem: each evaluation returns a single score, allowing the tuner to learn which configuration is faster, but not why. Inspired by the use of profilers in GPU-kernel optimization, we introduce APEC (Agent for Per-instance Explainable Configuration), a log-grounded tuning agent for MIP solvers. APEC has three layers: a deterministic layer that profiles each log, an interpretation layer that guides hypothesis-driven diagnosis, and a system layer that controls evaluation, enabling more reliable and interpretable solver tuning.
